newsitem.title: USA: Stocks gain, led by good earnings news.
newsitem.headline: Stocks gain, led by good earnings news.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were higher Monday, pleased with second-quarter earnings reports and heartened by a continued surge in the technology sector.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 16.72 points at 7,938.54.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 15-11 on heavy volume of 268 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laced with technology stocks, gained 18.00 points to 1,520.62 after closing last Friday above the 1,500 level for the first time.
"The excitement of earnings season is kicking in and the general feeling is for more surprises on the upside than on the downside," said Robert Froelich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.
A powerful rally in the shares of big-name technology companies also gave upward momentum to the broader market, analysts said.
"Intel's up, Microsoft's up and the semiconductor stocks are strong," said Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt.
Intel Corp. rose two to 78-7/8 after its stock split two for one. Microsoft Corp. gained 3-1/16 to 132-13/16, and Dell Computer Corp. rose 3-3/4 to 141-3/4.

"Tech stocks are really flying," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "The feeling is that the worst of the slowdown is over. Aggressive portfolio managers determined to get performance are also concentrating on this high-momentum area."
A rosy outlook for the economy, with tame inflation, moderate growth and low inflation, was also boosting stocks.

The market will be weighing the latest economic numbers at mid-week. The Consumer Price Index for June, an indication of inflation is due Wednesday. It was expected to rise 0.2 percent, compared with a 0.1 percent gain in May.
Industrial production for June was also slated to come out Wednesday. It was expected to rise 0.2 percent vs. a 0.4 percent gain in May.

"We have had a run of extraordinarily positive economic and inflation data," said Alfred Kugel, Stein Roe & Farnham senior investment strategist. "There is nothing to disturb investors and traders can't find a reason to sell."
So far, most corporate earnings had come in as forecast, contributing to the positive sentiment, analysts said.

NationsBank Corp. rose 1-5/16 to 67-15/16 after posting second-quarter earnings of $1.05 per share vs. $1.00 per share a year earlier. Analysts' consensus earnings estimate for NationsBank was $1.00 per share.
First Chicago NBD Corp. gained 1-1/16 to 64-1/16 after it reported quarterly earnings of $1.20 vs. $1.09 per share a year ago.

Brokerage firm Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. said its second-quarter income rose to a record $100.2 million, topping a previous record of $97.0 million set in the comparable period last year. Its stock added 2-11/16 to 59-1/4.
But HCIA Inc.'s stock sank 16-7/16 to 15-9/16, after it forecast a second-quarter loss.
